newsitem.title: USA: Stocks off on profit taking; interest rate jitters.
newsitem.headline: Stocks off on profit taking; interest rate jitters.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell on profit-taking Monday after posting their biggest weekly gain ever last week.
The market also was rattled by fresh interest rates jitters after a Federal Reserve official warned that the possibility of "overheating" was the major threat to the economy.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 43.34 points at 6,660.21, giving back some of the ground from last week's 312-point rally, which was the 30-stock index's largest weekly surge.

For the second time in as many weeks, the New York Stock Exchange handled its lowest trading volume of the year as only 393 million shares changed hands, barely beating the low of 407 million last Monday.
In the broader market, declining issues swamped advances 1,649 to 905.

"The volume numbers tell you buyers have really backed away here," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "It's not hard to figure out why. It's almost entirely a function of interest rates."
The 30-year Treasury bond was off 14/32, raising its yield to 7.09 percent from Friday's close of 7.05 percent. The price and yield move in opposite directions.

Financial markets were again uneasy about another rise in interest rates after Federal Reserve Board Vice Chairwoman Alice Rivlin said the major threat to the economy at the moment was the possibility of over-heating.
"The major threat at the moment is not that the economy will run out of steam (but) that's always possible," Rivlin said in a speech to the Employment Policy Foundation.
"The thing that worries the Federal Reserve more is the possible overheating of the economy," she said.
The technology stocks were hammered again.

"The tech stocks participated in the rally last week for about 15 minutes," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "And this market is in a near-term downtrend regardless of last week's rally."

The stocks of networking companies were among the hardest-hit in the tech sector, with Cisco Systems Inc., down 1-1/16 to 47-5/16, 3Com Corp. off 2-7/8 to 26-3/8 and Ascend Communications Inc. off 2 to 38-1/4.
The Nasdaq Composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, fell 18.62 points to 1,203.95.
Financial stocks also were broadly lower, with Chase Manhattan Corp. down 2 to 85-1/2 and J.P. Morgan & Co. shedding 1-1/2 to 95-3/8.
With interest rates again thrust onto centre stage, again, analysts said stocks could find themselves back on shaky footing if evidence favours another Federal Reserve rate hike.
The central bank last month raised interest rates for the first time in more than two years, citing the need to head off inflation.
Oil company stocks were among the few to largely shrug off the weak tone in the market as giants Amoco Corp., Amerada Hess Corp. and Exxon Corp. all reported earnings that beat Wall Street estimates.
Hess shares rose 3/8 to 49-1/8 and Amoco gained 5/8 to 82. Exxon shares shed 1/8, however, finishing at 53-3/8 after gaining more than 2 initially.

Among individual stocks, AutoImmune Inc. plunged 9-7/16 or 69 percent to 4-5/16 after the company announced a Phase III trial showed no difference in patient response to its multiple sclerosis drug Myloral and a placebo.
APAC TeleServices Inc. slid 10-3/8 to 11-1/8 after it reported lower-than-expected first quarter earnings.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks lost 5.97 points to 760.37. The American Stock Exchange index was off 4.54 to 551.47.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 3.24 to 399.40. The average share was down 32 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,198.918 down 70.548 or 0.97 percent.
